newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Oil Search reports 800m Moran oil column.
newsitem.headline: Oil Search reports 800m Moran oil column.

text.p: Partners in the Moran oil field in Papua New Guinea said on Wednesday the Moran-2X sidetrack well has intersected a vertical oil column of 800 metres.

Analysts said the result supported predictions by Oil Search Ltd, which has a 7.76 percent stake in the field, that Moran may hold more oil than the nearby Kutubu field, which has recoverable reserves of 305 million barrels of oil.
"It will give them a lot of confidence that the well has the potential to contain in excess of the amount that is in Kutubu," said James Capel analyst Stuart Smith.
Oil Search managing director Peter Botten said in March Moran could start producing 10,000 barrels of oil a day as early as September this year.
The Moran-2X sidetrack well, designed to test the downdip extent of oil located earlier in the Toro and Digimu structures, reached a final depth of 4,176 metres.

Oil Search said wireline logs indicated oil-water contact in the Toro C sandstone about 180 metres below the lowest known oil intersected in earlier drilling, and oil water contact in the Digimu sandstone about 170 metres below that intersected earlier.
"The total vertical oil column intersected in the Digimu sandstone at Moran is now approximately 800 metres," Oil Search said.
Analysts said it was too early to give an estimate of potential reserves, but said the result would put some limits on the upside for the field.
"It may have punctured some of the extreme expectations that were in the market," said Macquarie Equities oil and gas analyst Peter Best.
Operator Chevron unit Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd, which has a 19.375 percent stake, plans to drill a second sidetrack well and two further appraisal wells, Oil Search said.

The PDL-2 licence holders are: Oil Search 7.763 percent, Chevron and The British Petroleum Co Plc 19.375 percent each, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd 9.688 percent, Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd 16.455 percent, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd affiliate Japan Papua New Guinea Petroleum Co Ltd (JPP) 4.844 percent, Orogen Minerals (Ltd 15.75 percent and Petroleum Resources Kutubu Pty Ltd 6.75 percent.

Brokers said Oil Search shares eased early in the day on speculation the well may have been unsuccessful, but regained ground. Oil Search shares were seven cents lower at A$3.37 at 4.15 p.m. (0615 GMT). Orogen was up one cent at A$3.86.
